summary: Flathead National Forest lookout above Swan Lake, rebuilt in 1959 after earlier platform towers, now a Forest Service rental cabin.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab, 41-foot treated timber tower

access.note: drive-up to parking area, then climb tower stairs

visit.trail_note: parking area adjacent to tower; steep stairway to climb

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Flathead National Forest

events.note: 25-foot platform tower, the first lookout structure on the site
cabin for living quarters and a newer 35-foot wooden platform added in the 1930s
current 41-foot R-6 flat-cab treated timber tower built
registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, December 30, 2020

evidence.supports: 1921 platform tower, 1930s cabin/platform, 1959 current tower, R-6 flat cab design
evidence.quote: A 25' platform tower was built in 1921, with a cabin for living quarters built in the 1930's along with a newer, 35' wooden platform. The present tower, a 41' treated timber with R-6 flat cab, built in 1959, is still used for emergencies

evidence.supports: 75 years as fire detection site; rental cabin facilities and access details
evidence.quote: The site served for 75 years as a fire detection tower, and the current lookout has been around since its construction in 1959. The 15-by-15 facility sits atop a 40-foot tower. It is equipped with a built-in double bed and two folding cots, to accommodate up to four adults. The lookout also has a propane cooking stove, simple cooking utensils and a table with four chairs. A modern vault toilet, picnic area and fire ring are located at the base of the tower. No water or electricity is available. Grizzly bears frequent the area; use appropriate containers for food and garbage. The lookout is a 40-foot tower and guests must be prepared to climb and carry provisions up the steep stairway; due to the height of the tower, children under age 10 are discouraged. The cabin remains locked; a combination lock code will be contained in the reservation confirmation letter.
Known lookout personnel: 1957: Ewing Micken; 1958: Mr. & Mrs. Richard Beighle.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR brief notes sources differ because some count the original 1921 platform tower and others the 1959 structure now on site; both figures appear consistently across sources checked here so no further conflict found

notes_for_editor: Brief's conflict note about differing build years is explained by NHLR's own description distinguishing the 1921 platform from the 1959 cab; no discrepancy found between the three sources checked.
